items.context: 5 client files (tidiness_manager, test_genie, auditor, browser_automation, agent_manager) each duplicate doJSON(), doGet(), resolveBaseURL(), and error parsing. This accounts for a large portion of the complexity and duplication violations. The question is how to share this logic.

options.label: Embedded struct composition
options.rationale: Create a BaseClient struct with shared methods (doJSON, doGet, resolveBaseURL). Each service client embeds BaseClient. Error parsing uses a configurable service name. Minimal API surface change, idiomatic Go composition. Recommended because it's simple, doesn't over-abstract, and matches Go conventions.

options.label: Standalone helper functions
options.rationale: Extract doJSON/doGet as package-level functions that accept an http.Client and base URL. Simpler but requires passing client/URL to every call, and error parsing still needs per-service customization.

items.topic: Test refactoring scope for this item
items.context: The biggest test file is gitignore_health_service_test.go (441 lines, 85% duplication). Other test files (ssh/service_test.go, handler tests) have moderate duplication. Converting all tests to table-driven + helpers is thorough but increases scope. We could focus only on the worst offenders to hit the <10 targets.

options.label: Refactor all test files with duplication >50%
options.rationale: Comprehensive approach that addresses all test duplication. More work but ensures we comfortably hit the targets and the improvements are durable.

options.label: Only refactor files individually exceeding thresholds
options.rationale: Focus on files that individually contribute to complex_functions or long_files violations. Faster, but may leave borderline files that push us over the targets.

items.context: golang/scanner.go and python/scanner.go have ~90% identical Scan() bodies. They differ only in which matcher functions they call and which import field they extract. With only 2 language scanners and each file being ~50-60 lines, the duplication is real but the files are small.

options.label: Extract shared ScanImports helper function
options.rationale: Create a shared function like ScanImports(ctx, content, matchers) that handles context cancellation and import aggregation. Each scanner calls it with its language-specific matchers. Simple, no over-engineering.

options.label: Leave as-is — files are small enough
options.rationale: Each file is ~50-60 lines. The duplication is real but the cognitive overhead of an abstraction may not be worth it for just 2 scanners. Accept the duplication score hit.

items.context: There are 2 TODO comments in UI files: App.tsx:1320 ('TODO: Use lineNumber to scroll to the specific line') and ScenarioReviewPanel.tsx:665 ('TODO: Remove this client-side fallback once the unified review endpoint is stable'). These are the only tech_debt_markers counted.

options.label: Implement the TODO functionality and remove markers
options.rationale: Actually implement scroll-to-line and remove the client-side fallback if the unified endpoint is stable. Most thorough but adds UI implementation scope to a Go refactoring task.

options.label: Remove TODOs as comments, file separate backlog items
options.rationale: Delete the TODO comments to clear the markers. Create separate backlog items for the actual work. Keeps this item focused on Go refactoring.

items.text: The duplication_pct reported by tidiness-manager is very high (85-100%) across most files. This is driven primarily by the HTTP client pattern repeated in 5 files and the test setup boilerplate. Addressing the shared HTTP client alone should dramatically reduce the complex_functions count since each client contributes ~3-4 complex functions (doJSON, doGet, error parser, plus wrapper methods).

plan_updates: Created initial plan.md scaffold with 4 implementation phases (shared HTTP client, test helpers, scanner abstraction, tech debt markers), full file inventory, risk matrix, and acceptance criteria aligned with the success targets.
